Definition: from G4951; a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), i.e. the Syrtis Major or great bay on the north coast of Africa:--quicksands.
BiblicalUsage: The Syrtis was the great shoal off the north coast of Africa, a stretch of shallow sandbanks that sailors feared more than open sea. When the storm drove Paul's ship, the crew struck sail and let her drift, afraid of running aground on the Syrtis. Luke names the danger plainly, and the fear in the verse is real: a ship on the Syrtis was a ship lost.
TheologicalSignificance: One verse shows how honestly Luke writes about danger, I believe. The crew did what they could, and God still brought them through; fear and faith sit side by side in the same storm.
